objective: Given a U.S. location, today's date and optional gardener-managed conditions, tell a serious home gardener what can be started today, by which method, what can be repeated, when the opportunity closes, what harvest is realistic, and what can occupy the bed next—while being honest about climate, crop biology and protection uncertainty.
scoreFormula: Value score = sum(weight × category_rating/100). Final score = max(0, value score - triggered loss penalties). Ship only when final score >= 92, every critical category >= 85, all automatic rejects are false, and required scenario tests pass.

valueFunctions.definition: Crop recommendations respect crop biology, frost sensitivity, season, sowing method, transplant sensitivity, maturity and source-backed agronomic rules.
The engine directly answers whether planting today can still produce a realistic harvest, using method-specific maturity, cold deadline, seasonal slowdown, and alternate harvest modes where valid.
Repeat sowings are computed conditionally from today and stop when the next sowing no longer fits; projected harvest can trigger realistic same-bed follow-on crops.
Fall schedules work backward from local cold risk, add slower autumn growth and safety time, and do not treat the first 32F event as the universal end for hardy crops.
Indoor start, direct sow, hardening and transplant are distinct; method-specific days-to-harvest are supported and transplant-sensitive crops are not routinely transplanted.
NOAA freeze probability anchors and the current NWS forecast are separate inputs; USDA hardiness is context only.

Optional measured soil temperature can block premature direct sowing, live forecast heat can caution or pause cool-season planting, and actual forecast minimum can stop a crop at its modeled injury threshold.

User-declared row cover or low-tunnel assumptions extend only defensible cool-season windows, never rewrite ambient forecast temperatures, and never make tender crops frost-proof; temporary shade can manage heat establishment without erasing heat risk.
Users can override generic maturity with seed-packet days; the engine can distinguish full maturity from legitimate baby-leaf, greens or young-root harvests.
Frost-light and subtropical locations become heat-limited cool-season calendars, with managed establishment options, rather than failing or imitating a northern calendar.
Probability anchors, station fit, live forecast, protection assumptions and planning buffers are labeled rather than presented as exact guarantees.
The first screen exposes direct sow now, transplant now, start indoors, last-call/quick harvest, fall opportunities, conditional next succession and optional season-extension controls.
Crop rules are structured, source-keyed, testable outside the page, and the canonical URL is preserved.

lossFunctions.trigger: Recommends a frost-tender crop outdoors despite current freeze risk or after its viable cold deadline.
Row cover/low-tunnel selection makes a tender crop frost-proof, rewrites the NWS forecast temperature, or overrides an actual modeled crop injury threshold.
Uses USDA hardiness zone as the primary planting-date engine.
Produces a single spring schedule with no computed fall or succession behavior.
Routinely recommends transplanting a transplant-sensitive root crop.
Says there is nothing useful to plant now when source-backed crops still have realistic seasonal runway.
Uses spring days-to-maturity unchanged for fall cutoffs without slowdown or safety allowance.
Recommends cool crops through severe forecast heat or warm direct-seeded crops into a user-entered soil temperature below the crop minimum without warning/blocking.
Presents first/last frost as a guaranteed date.
Displays repeated sowing dates after the last viable planting window.
Creates thin city/ZIP pages instead of strengthening the canonical decision tool.
